plan: This is a second-price sealed-bid auction (highest bidder wins, pays second-highest bid). In such auctions, the dominant strategy is to bid one's true value, since the payment doesn't depend on your own bid (given you win), only on the second-highest bid. Bidding above value risks overpaying; bidding below value risks losing profitable opportunities. Since my value is $4, I should bid exactly $4, regardless of what I think others will bid - this is optimal regardless of their strategies.

In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of the number of competitors or their strategies. This holds because the winner pays the second-highest bid, not their own bid, so misrepresenting your value only risks losing profitable trades or winning unprofitable ones. Since my value is $23, bidding exactly $23 maximizes expected profit: I win whenever my value exceeds the second-highest bid, and pay only that amount, ensuring non-negative surplus whenever I win.

This is a second-price (Vickrey) auction: the winner pays the second-highest bid, not their own bid. In such auctions, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of other bidders' behavior—overbidding risks paying more than the item is worth, while underbidding risks losing profitable opportunities without any benefit. Since my value is $32, I should bid exactly $32 to maximize expected profit, as this strategy is optimal no matter what the other rational bidders do.
